turn_text: My guest at this time is Florida Republican Congressman Ted Yoho. He represents Florida's Third Congressional District. He's also on both the House Foreign Affairs and Agriculture Committees. He's also on the Western Hemisphere, Civilian Security and Trade Subcommittee for the Foreign Affairs Panel. And he is the lead sponsor for a new piece of legislation that essentially creates some new rules, new parameters for agricultural guest workers. And Congressman, thanks so much for being with us.
Hey Greg, thanks for having me on.

Absolutely. Well, we obviously have guest worker programs already and agricultural workers are a big part of that. Talk about your philosophy before we get into some of the specifics here. Why did you decide to tackle this? Why do you think there needs to be these changes to the existing plan?

Because the existing plan is broken. And that's one of the reasons we have such a mess on our immigration. And what I've learned in my seven years up there is you can have an immigration debate in Washington. And so we've taken the debate from immigration to really focus on that solution to what we need. And we need a guest worker program that'll provide predictable and a steady flow of migrant labor in the areas where we need them. And we're looking at the lower-end skilled works. And I'm focused on the agriculture sector. And so we wanted to have a predictable, reliable, and certain workforce coming in. We wanted a way for the people that want to come in and work in our agricultural sector to be able to come in legally so that they don't have to cross across our southern border illegally and pay a coyote and risk their families life at it. And we've accomplished that. So we've solved the problem for our producers and we've solved the problem for the people wanting to come in and work legally in this country.

turn_text: One big part of this though, and it's certainly a big part of what I've seen in your materials here, is making sure this is done in a secure way that protects national security. So explain what you would require guest workers to do once they come in here and looking for jobs in the agriculture sector.

Okay, first we move ag labor from the department labor to the USDA and let them run this program. People are pre-screened before they come into the country. Meaning that say if somebody wants to come in from Honduras, we have an agreement between the country of Honduras and our State Department. The country of Honduras will verify this person is who they say they are basically passport information. And then in addition, they'll have a letter certification. This person's not wanted for drugs, gang member, violent crimes. So we've pre-screened people before they have applied. During the application process, though, the applicant, they don't come into the country until a job is available. But before a job is available, that information goes from the State Department to the Department of Homeland Security, where they do a background check. If they clear that, that information goes to the USDA. When that person comes into the country, they become now a participant when a job is available. They pay a $2,500 fee for a five year period of time, meaning they can stay in this country for five years at a time. They can renew four and a half years into it. They have to be a minimum of 18 years of age to apply. They apply individually. They don't apply, you know, and bring a family. And then they get entered, Greg. This is probably the strongest part of this. They get entered into the eVerify system before they come into the country. So now our employers can take legal workers that are already in the government e-verify system and they can utilize the e-verify system. Right now we don't have a good way to have enough workers in the e-verify system. And the last thing is the workers that come in in their permit number will have the initials AG for agriculture, meaning they have agreed to come in and work and only work in the agriculture sector.
